intent: Two brisk small affirmative nods, second smaller, with supported connected body acting
primaryMotion:
Umi hears something he agrees with and answers his friend with two natural small nods of recognition. His alert gaze meets his friend; the first clear head dip arrives promptly at normal everyday speed, around0.2–0.35seconds, and recovers with supported weight. After a short living pause, a smaller second nod gently confirms the same thought. The two accents have different weight and spacing. Do not stretch either small dip across the entire four-second shot. Eyes and eyelids, the head and neck, chest and relaxed shoulders accommodate the SAME intention together, so this reads as a seated animal acknowledging his friend rather than a head being mechanically translated over a rigid body. Let a quick natural blink belong to the acknowledgement, with continuous dark eyelid lines and separate small gray bean eyebrows; reopen the same blue star eyes. The tiny friendly animal smile remains restrained, with no talking or new teeth.

Both full ROUND gray paws stay comfortably planted at their original support line. Their thick white furry forearms and compact short wrists support the chest response without sliding, shrinking, opening or turning either paw toward the camera. Preserve the natural compact rounded animal digits and tiny ivory claw tips through correct overlap; do not lengthen or display human fingers. The lower seated body and grounded paw contact do not travel. Preserve the original face width, head/body ratio, gray/white pointed fur borders and original material colors. The folded hood-ear tip and scarf can give a brief small after-settle from the same nod, while the single heavy cape and its narrow lower corners remain draped downward and grounded, never spreading into wings. Return naturally to the supplied original supported open-eyed pose and compatible breathing phase for a forward loop, without a frozen ending or snap. No whole-image scaling, camera movement, floating support, metronomic rocking, slow motion, or separately demonstrated limbs.
